chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When a man gives a charity (sadaqah), it is not permissible for him to buy it back, nor to ask for it as a gift, nor to reclaim it, except in the case of inheritance."

key_terms.صَدَقَة: Charity, voluntary alms given for the sake of God
key_terms.يَسْتَوْهِبَهَا: To ask for it as a gift (reclaiming via gift)

ai.seo_question: Can a person buy back or reclaim their own charity after giving it?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies that a voluntary charity (sadaqah) becomes irrevocable upon possession by the recipient, preventing the donor from reclaiming it through purchase (shira'), gift (istwahab), or direct recovery (istiradd), except in the specific case of inheritance. This ruling underscores the permanence of the transfer of ownership, distinguishing sadaqah from other forms of gift-giving where revocation might be permissible, and highlights the legal mechanism by which a donor might indirectly recover the value if the recipient passes away and the charity is part of the estate.
